title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Hormuz got worse over the weekend: a UAE-owned products tanker burned off Khasab, UKMTO logged 11 attacks in a week, and traffic is about a fifth of pre-war. The long-term answer moved a step closer on Sunday, when all six GCC states signed the Gulf Railway agreement.

stories.headline: A UAE-owned tanker burns off Khasab as Iran steps up attacks on Hormuz shipping
body: A products tanker, tentatively identified as the Navig8 Messi and indirectly owned by ADNOC L&S, caught fire about eight nautical miles off Khasab on Saturday evening. The crew was evacuated with no injuries. The IRGC said three tankers caught fire on Sunday after using "unauthorised routes", and it claims at least 12 ships have burned this month, mostly from mines.

UKMTO confirmed eight attacks in the strait and three in the Arabian Gulf over the past week; three vessels sank. The UAE National Guard rescued 22 crew from a burning cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman. Traffic is about 20% of pre-war, and the US disabled the Iran-linked bulker Huda in the Gulf of Oman on 7 November.
stories.soWhat: New since Friday: a UAE-linked ship hit right at the strait, and three sinkings in a week. Keep sea war-risk surcharges Gulf-wide and push east-coast and overland routings.
stories.source: The National; Maritime Executive; Gulf News

stories.headline: GCC states sign the Gulf Railway agreement: 1,700 km from Kuwait to Oman
body: The six GCC transport ministers signed the General Agreement for the GCC Railway Project in Bahrain on 8 November. The network targets 200 million tonnes of freight by 2030 and full operations in December 2030. Core infrastructure is put at $15.4–16 billion.

The GCC Railways Authority says overall completion has passed 50%. Hafeet Rail, the 238 km UAE–Oman link, is about 40% complete with trials targeted for Q4 2027. The full text of the agreement has not been published.
stories.soWhat: Rail will not help this quarter, but Hormuz makes overland Gulf corridors a lasting product. Start planning rail-linked GCC freight offers with Etihad Rail.

stories.headline: Saudi air links: flydubai returns to Dammam from 10 November; Riyadh and Abha from 17 November
body: flydubai's Riyadh and Abha flights stay suspended through 16 November, with Dammam available again from 10 November. Etihad has cancelled all passenger and cargo flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh and Dammam until 19 November; its Jeddah flights resumed on 6 November. Dubai International also reported six flynas cancellations to Riyadh and Gassim.
stories.soWhat: New: Dubai–Dammam belly space returns tomorrow. Riyadh stays road-only from the UAE for at least another week.

stories.headline: Air cargo spot rates keep climbing; Gulf capacity still 19% short
body: WorldACD says global spot rates rose 5% in the week of 19–25 October to $3.80 per kilo, 38% above last year, even as tonnage fell 2%. Middle East and South Asia capacity is 13% below late February, and Arabian Gulf capacity 19% below. Riyadh was almost completely closed to international flights that week.
stories.soWhat: Buy rates are still rising into peak. Price air sell rates weekly, not monthly.

stories.headline: Oil eases to $97.67 as Trump plays down new strikes
body: Brent was at $97.67 a barrel on Monday morning, down 64 cents, and briefly fell more than $1 at the open. WTI was at $90.51. Trump told CNN new strikes on Iran were "highly unlikely" to be necessary if talks progress, but Iran's foreign minister said no negotiations have taken place since the US midterms.
stories.soWhat: Oil is stuck near $98 with no deal in sight. Keep December fuel surcharges where they are.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Launches 'AI Tech', a dedicated product for AI server racks and chips
body: Emirates SkyCargo launched AI Tech on 3 November for AI server racks, semiconductors, GPUs and capital equipment, with priority loading and proactive monitoring. It says it moved more than 700 tonnes of AI infrastructure in July alone, and will run 23 freighters by March 2027.
competitors.soWhat: Same week, same target as our Data Center Logistics launch. SkyCargo owns the lift; we must win on end-to-end handling and site delivery.

competitors.name: noon & Amazon
competitors.headline: 11.11 enters its final days with bank and BNPL offers stacked on top
body: Amazon's sale ends on 12 November and noon's on 13 November. noon has added Emirates Islamic card discounts from 9 to 12 November and Tabby offers from 8 to 12 November, on top of 15-minute noon Minutes and 90-minute Supermall delivery.
competitors.soWhat: New: a last-week volume spike on 11–13 November. Expect returns to peak the week after; offer reverse logistics to sellers now.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Launched Data Center Logistics on 1 November
body: Aramex Data Center Logistics went live on 1 November in the GCC, Southeast Asia, Taiwan and the US South. It covers construction cargo such as transformers and chillers, AI racks by charter or secure road, white-glove handling in the data hall, and spare parts. A crated AI rack weighs about 1.75 tonnes. Q2 revenue was a record AED 1.83 billion; Q3 results are not yet out.
competitors.soWhat: A clear growth product. Pricing should set charter and white-glove rate cards before the first tenders.

opportunities.title: Dubai–Dammam air reopens
opportunities.text: flydubai is back on Dammam from 10 November. Re-open air offers to shippers who moved to road.

opportunities.title: UAE–Riyadh road freight
opportunities.text: Riyadh air stays cut to at least 16–19 November. Keep selling trucking on the lane.

opportunities.title: AI and data centre cargo
opportunities.text: Our new product and SkyCargo's both target it. Move fast on Abu Dhabi and Riyadh projects.

opportunities.title: Overland GCC corridors
opportunities.text: The Gulf Railway deal and Hormuz both point to land routes. Build multimodal GCC offers.

opportunities.title: Post-11.11 returns
opportunities.text: Sales end 12–13 November. Pitch returns handling to marketplace sellers this week.

watchouts.title: Sinkings in Hormuz
watchouts.text: Three vessels sank in a week, and a UAE-linked tanker was hit. Sea risk is rising, not easing.

watchouts.title: No talks
watchouts.text: Iran says no negotiations since the midterms. Oil can jump again at any time.

watchouts.title: Air rates still rising
watchouts.text: Spot up 38% on the year. Fixed-price air quotes can lose money fast.

watchouts.title: Big rival in AI cargo
watchouts.text: Emirates SkyCargo launched AI Tech the same week as us, with 23 freighters by March.

watchouts.title: Peak capacity squeeze
watchouts.text: 11.11 final days, then White Friday on 27 November. Last-mile capacity will be tight.

moves.title: Keep war-risk surcharges Gulf-wide
moves.text: Three sinkings and a hit off Khasab. No cuts this month.

moves.title: Hold December fuel surcharges
moves.text: Brent is near $98 with no talks. Hold until a deal is real.

moves.title: Restart Dubai–Dammam air offers
moves.text: flydubai flies again from 10 November. Call shippers who switched to road.

moves.title: Price air weekly
moves.text: Spot rates rose again. Move key air quotes to weekly validity through peak.

moves.title: Publish data centre rate cards
moves.text: Set charter and white-glove pricing before SkyCargo's AI Tech wins the first tenders.

moves.title: Sell post-11.11 returns
moves.text: Offer returns pick-up to sellers outside Amazon and noon fulfilment.
